**An exact tree split depends on ordering, not the numerical spacing between values.** If positive values are 1, 2, and 100, a threshold separating the first two from the last creates the same partition after applying log or cube. A strictly increasing transform preserves every comparison, so the same candidate left/right partitions remain available. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html)

The transformed threshold need not numerically match the old threshold, but it represents the same partition. Under ideal exact splitting with the same tie handling, split gains and predictions can therefore remain unchanged.

**Other models use more than order.** KNN uses distances, so compressing 100 with a logarithm changes its relative proximity. Linear regression on log(x) describes a curved relationship in original x, not the original linear hypothesis class. Neural-network representations and optimization can also change.

Practical tree implementations may use approximate histogram bins, random thresholds, finite precision, or tie conventions that break exact invariance. Missing values and categorical encodings add separate considerations. Most importantly, this argument concerns a feature transformation, not transforming the target. Fit learned preprocessing only on training data and use transforms only where they are defined. Tree scale invariance is a useful property with assumptions, not permission to ignore all preprocessing.

**Technical details and references.**

A strictly increasing transform preserves feature order, so an exact tree splitter can form the same left/right partitions with transformed thresholds. Log on positive values and cube are examples. In ideal arithmetic the fitted partitions are unchanged. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html)

Histogram binning, finite precision, ties, random thresholds, and implementation details can break exact practical invariance. The result also says nothing about changing the **target**.

Linear regression changes its hypothesis class from linear-in-$x$ to linear-in-$f(x)$. kNN distances change, and neural optimization/representations can change. Fit transforms only where mathematically defined and use training-only learned parameters. Tree invariance does not mean preprocessing is irrelevant: missing values, categorical encoding, and leakage still matter.
